title: Nonacute angles and defect matching
subtitle: G2 lecture 050000 · expanded mathematical companion
adaptation: Standalone companion adapted from the source spoken lecture and display-only mathematics appendix. Explicit hypotheses, stepwise proofs, worked examples, and local vector diagrams; no narration edits.

slides.title: What fails at a right angle?
slides.lead: A right-angle principal direction has cosine zero, so the projection-built transport K loses that direction.
body: The polar factor of K transports all surviving, nonperpendicular directions, but it cannot supply a unitary on the exact crossed defects by itself.
The missing part is a matching problem. We must pair the source-only perpendicular directions with the target-only perpendicular directions and rotate each matched pair by a quarter-turn.
slides.takeaway: The failure of cosine invertibility identifies a concrete defect-matching task.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 050000 · What fails at a right angle?

slides.title: Name the two crossed defect spaces
slides.lead: The source defect contains directions of U perpendicular to V; the target defect contains directions of V perpendicular to U.
body: Write D_s=U∩V⊥ and D_t=U⊥∩V. These spaces are orthogonal because D_s lies in U and D_t in U⊥.
A unitary direct rotation must carry the source defect to the target defect. Accordingly their Hilbert-space dimensions must match, including infinite cardinal dimension.
slides.takeaway: Direct rotation requires compatible source and target right-angle defects.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 050000 · Name the two crossed defect spaces

slides.title: The simplest right-angle plane
slides.lead: Take U as the horizontal axis and V as the vertical axis in the real plane.
body: Here P and Q project onto perpendicular lines, and K=QP+(I−Q)(I−P)=0 on the whole plane. The regular polar construction provides no transport there.
But a quarter-turn sends the horizontal axis onto the vertical one and is unitary. The missing information is exactly the choice of which perpendicular directions are matched.
slides.takeaway: An exact right angle requires a chosen quarter-turn on the defect plane.

slides.title: Choose an isometry between the defects
slides.lead: Assume an isometric isomorphism J:D_s→D_t has been chosen.
body: On D_s⊕D_t define T_J(x,y)=(-J*y,Jx). It sends source defects into target defects and target defects back with the negative adjoint.
This is the operator analogue of a quarter-turn on each matched pair. It is skew-adjoint and squares to minus the identity on the defect sum.
slides.takeaway: A chosen defect isometry determines a length-preserving quarter-turn.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 050000 · Choose an isometry between the defects

slides.title: Split the regular and defect pieces
slides.lead: The crossed defects form an orthogonal reducing summand for both projections.
body: Let D=D_s⊕D_t and R=D⊥. On R, the canonical intertwiner K has no crossed defect kernel. Its polar factor is unitary on the regular part.
On D use the quarter-turn T_J. Since the two pieces are orthogonal and reducing, the direct sum of the regular polar factor and T_J is a unitary on the entire ambient space.
slides.takeaway: Regular angles use the polar factor; exact right angles use defect matching.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 050000 · Split the regular and defect pieces

slides.title: Why the dimensions must agree
slides.lead: A quarter-turn between D_s and D_t cannot be unitary unless the two spaces are isometrically equivalent.
body: If a direct rotation has the required off-diagonal quarter-turn structure on D, its restriction must be a surjective isometry from one defect space to the other.
Conversely, choosing such an isometry provides the explicit block T_J. This proves necessity and sufficiency of the matching condition for this canonical direct-rotation construction.
slides.takeaway: The existence obstruction is an isometric mismatch of the two crossed defects.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 050000 · Why the dimensions must agree

slides.title: Equal ambient dimensions do not settle the issue
slides.lead: In infinite dimensions, proper subspaces can have the same infinite dimension as the whole space.
body: Let H=ℓ²(N), U=H, and V the range of the unilateral shift. Both U and V are infinite-dimensional, yet U∩V⊥ is one-dimensional while U⊥∩V=0.
Thus a unitary of H cannot send U=H onto the proper subspace V, and the defect dimensions expose the obstruction immediately.
slides.takeaway: In infinite Hilbert spaces, matching global dimensions is weaker than matching crossed defects.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 050000 · Equal ambient dimensions do not settle the issue

slides.title: Finite-dimensional matching is concrete
slides.lead: When the defect spaces are finite-dimensional, the matching condition reduces to equality of their dimensions.
body: Choose orthonormal bases e₁,…,e_m of D_s and f₁,…,f_m of D_t. Define J e_i=f_i and extend linearly; its adjoint sends f_i back to e_i.
The block T_J is then a direct sum of m ordinary ninety-degree rotations. The remaining regular principal planes are rotated through their non-right-angle amounts.
slides.takeaway: One matched basis pair supplies one quarter-turn block.

slides.title: What remains canonical?
slides.lead: The regular polar factor is specified intrinsically by P and Q, but the right-angle matching is not unique.
body: If dim D_s=dim D_t>1, many different unitary isomorphisms J exist. Each supplies a different direct rotation that agrees on the regular part and differs only in the defect block.
The construction therefore identifies exactly where nonuniqueness enters: the pair of subspaces does not prescribe a preferred matching of orthogonal source and target directions.
slides.takeaway: Nonuniqueness at right angles is localized to the choice of defect isometry.

slides.title: Reconstruct the completion
slides.lead: A correct argument has to keep the regular polar factor and the defect quarter-turn separate.
body: Show that K vanishes on D_s⊕D_t. Verify T_J*T_J=I and T_J²=−I, then check how T_J exchanges the two defect spaces.
Finally assemble the orthogonal direct sum with the polar factor on R. This reproduces the direct-rotation existence criterion without pretending that zero cosine can be inverted.
slides.takeaway: A direct rotation across right angles is a polar factor plus an explicit matching block.
